# DITA XML Structure Validation Skill

## Overview
This skill provides a structured validation checklist for DITA XML output generated by the Draft-doc agent. Use this to catch common structural issues early, before content enters review or publication workflows.

## When to Use
- After drafting DITA XML content fragments (tasks, concepts, references, release notes, etc.)
- Before committing DITA topic files to the repository
- When reviewing generated markup for consistency with existing topic patterns
- To validate that generated elements will render correctly in DITA output

## Validation Checklist

### 1. Tag Integrity
- [ ] All opening tags have matching closing tags (e.g., `<p>...</p>`, `<step>...</step>`)
- [ ] No orphaned tags (e.g., `<li>` without `</li>`, `<entry>` without `</entry>`)
- [ ] Self-closing tags are avoided in DITA (use full open/close pairs)
- [ ] No extra closing tags or duplicate tag pairs
- [ ] Tag names use correct DITA element names and casing (lowercase: `<p>`, `<li>`, `<uicontrol>`)

### 2. DOCTYPE and Topic Structure
- [ ] DOCTYPE declaration matches topic type:
  - Concept: `<!DOCTYPE concept PUBLIC "-//OASIS//DTD DITA Concept//EN" "concept.dtd">`
  - Task: `<!DOCTYPE task PUBLIC "-//OASIS//DTD DITA Task//EN" "task.dtd">`
  - Reference: `<!DOCTYPE reference PUBLIC "-//OASIS//DTD DITA Reference//EN" "reference.dtd">`
  - Topic: `<!DOCTYPE topic PUBLIC "-//OASIS//DTD DITA Topic//EN" "topic.dtd">`
- [ ] Root element matches DOCTYPE (concept, task, reference, or topic)
- [ ] Root element has required attributes: `id` and `xml:lang="en"`
- [ ] Topic has one `<title>` element immediately after root
- [ ] Topic body matches type: `<conbody>`, `<taskbody>`, or `<refbody>`

### 3. Nesting and Hierarchy
- [ ] All nested elements are properly closed before their parent closes (no "crossing" tags)
  - ✗ Bad: `<p><uicontrol></p></uicontrol>`
  - ✓ Good: `<p><uicontrol>...</uicontrol></p>`
- [ ] Block-level elements (`<p>`, `<ol>`, `<ul>`, `<note>`) are not nested inside inline elements (`<uicontrol>`, `<codeph>`)
- [ ] Sections follow proper hierarchy (title → shortdesc → prolog → body)
- [ ] Prolog elements (if present) appear before topic body

### 4. Metadata and Prolog
- [ ] `<prolog>` element (if present) is between `<title>` and topic body
- [ ] `<metadata>` is inside `<prolog>`
- [ ] `<othermeta>` elements have both `name` and `content` attributes
- [ ] Common pattern: `<othermeta content="page-id" name="pageid"/>`

### 5. Title and Short Description
- [ ] Every topic has exactly one `<title>` element
- [ ] `<shortdesc>` appears after `<title>` or inside `<abstract>` element
- [ ] `<shortdesc>` contains a concise introductory sentence (not a heading)
- [ ] When `<title>` starts with a verb, use gerund form (e.g., "Configuring..." not "Configure...")

### 6. List Validation
- [ ] No empty list items (e.g., `<li></li>`)
- [ ] No direct text children of `<ul>`, `<ol>`, or `<dl>` (only list items)

### 7. Task-Specific Elements
- [ ] `<taskbody>` contains valid child elements in order:
  - Optional: `<prereq>`, `<context>`
  - Required: `<steps>` or `<steps-unordered>`
  - Optional: `<result>`, `<example>`, `<postreq>`
- [ ] `<steps>` contains one or more `<step>` elements
- [ ] Each `<step>` has a `<cmd>` (command) element
- [ ] Optional `<step>` children follow order: `<cmd>`, `<info>`, `<substeps>`, `<stepxmp>`, `<stepresult>`, `<tutorialinfo>`, `<choicetable>`
- [ ] `<substeps>` contains `<substep>` elements (each with its own `<cmd>`)
- [ ] Single-step procedures are avoided; use `<context>` with `<p>` instead

### 8. Concept-Specific Elements
- [ ] `<conbody>` contains block-level elements: `<p>`, `<ul>`, `<ol>`, `<note>`, `<fig>`, `<codeblock>`, `<section>`, etc.
- [ ] No `<steps>` or task-specific elements in concept topics

### 9. Reference-Specific Elements
- [ ] `<refbody>` contains appropriate reference content
- [ ] Reference topics often use `<simpletable>` for structured data

### 10. Table Structure (simpletable)
- [ ] `<simpletable>` uses DITA simple table structure (not HTML table)
- [ ] Optional `<simpletable>` attributes: `relcolwidth`, `frame`
- [ ] Optional header row uses `<sthead>` (simple table head)
- [ ] Data rows use `<strow>` (simple table row)
- [ ] Cells use `<stentry>` (simple table entry) - not `<td>` or `<th>`
- [ ] All rows have consistent column counts
- [ ] Table pattern:
  ```xml
  <simpletable relcolwidth="1.0* 2.0*">
    <sthead>
      <stentry>Column 1</stentry>
      <stentry>Column 2</stentry>
    </sthead>
    <strow>
      <stentry>Data 1</stentry>
      <stentry>Data 2</stentry>
    </strow>
  </simpletable>
  ```

### 11. Inline Elements and UI References
- [ ] UI elements use `<uicontrol>` (e.g., `<uicontrol>File</uicontrol>`)
- [ ] Menu cascades use `<menucascade>` with `<uicontrol>` children:
  - ✓ `<menucascade><uicontrol>File</uicontrol><uicontrol>Export</uicontrol></menucascade>`
- [ ] Window titles use `<wintitle>` (e.g., `<wintitle>Preferences</wintitle>`)
- [ ] Short code snippets use `<codeph>` (code phrase); longer blocks use `<codeblock>` with optional `translate="no"`
- [ ] User input uses `<userinput>` or `<filepath>` for file paths
- [ ] System output uses `<systemoutput>`
- [ ] No Markdown artifacts (no backticks, asterisks for bold/italic)

### 12. Cross-References and Links
- [ ] Internal references use `<xref>` with `href` attribute
- [ ] External links use `<xref>` with `format="html"` and `scope="external"`
- [ ] Link text is descriptive (no "click here")
- [ ] Content references use `<keyword>`, `<p>`, or `<ph>` with `conref` attribute
- [ ] Conref pattern: `<keyword conref="../../common/taxonomy/metadata-variables.dita#metadata-variables/42"/>`

### 13. Images
- [ ] Images use `<image>` element with `href` attribute
- [ ] All images have descriptive `<alt>` child element (not just `alt` attribute)
- [ ] Inline images use `placement="inline"` attribute
- [ ] Alt text includes punctuation unless image is an inline icon
- [ ] Pattern:
  ```xml
  <fig>
    <image href="../../common/images/example.png">
      <alt>Description of the image.</alt>
    </image>
  </fig>
  ```

### 14. Notes and Special Blocks
- [ ] Notes use `<note>` element (not `<div class="Note">`)
- [ ] Note types specified via `type` attribute: `note`, `tip`, `important`, `caution`, `warning`
- [ ] Output class filtering uses `outputclass` attribute with product IDs
- [ ] Pattern: `<note type="tip">Tip content here.</note>`

### 15. Code Blocks
- [ ] Code blocks use `<codeblock>` (not `<pre><code>`)
- [ ] Code blocks with code samples use `translate="no"` attribute
- [ ] Character escaping inside code blocks follows Section 16 guidelines
- [ ] Pattern:
  ```xml
  <codeblock translate="no">public void example() {
    return true;
  }</codeblock>
  ```

### 16. Character Encoding and Special Characters
- [ ] Special XML characters are properly escaped in text content:
  - `&lt;` for `<`
  - `&gt;` for `>`
  - `&amp;` for `&`
  - `&quot;` for `"`
  - `&apos;` for `'`
- [ ] No raw `<` or `>` characters in text (except in CDATA sections)
- [ ] Non-breaking spaces use `&#xA0;` or `&nbsp;` (use sparingly)
- [ ] Dashes: use en-dash `&#8211;` or em-dash `&#8212;` where appropriate

### 17. Semantic Markup
- [ ] Emphasis uses semantic elements, not `<b>`, `<i>`, or `<u>`
- [ ] Variables/placeholders use `<varname>` or `<parmname>`
- [ ] API names use `<apiname>`
- [ ] Options use `<option>`
- [ ] Command line commands use `<cmdname>`

### 18. DITA-Specific Attributes
- [ ] All file paths in `href` and `conref` use forward slashes `/` (not backslashes)
- [ ] Paths are relative to current file location
- [ ] Image paths point to `../../common/images/` or appropriate location
- [ ] Conref targets use format: `filepath#topicid/elementid`
- [ ] IDs use valid XML ID format (no spaces, starts with letter or underscore)

### 19. Talend-Specific Requirements
- [ ] Capitalize: Job, Joblet, subJob, Route, Routelet, Data Service, Flow (in DITA content)
- [ ] Use `<keyword conref="...">` for product names to ensure consistency
- [ ] Follow Qlik® trademark usage (first occurrence with ®)
- [ ] Sentence-style capitalization for all headings

### 20. Accessibility Validation
- [ ] All `<image>` elements have meaningful `<alt>` child elements
- [ ] Link text is descriptive and makes sense out of context
- [ ] Tables use `<sthead>` for header rows
- [ ] Color is not the only means of conveying information (add text cues)
- [ ] Procedural steps are in logical order

## Troubleshooting Invalid Output

When validation fails, cross-reference the symptom to the checklist section:

| Symptom | Checklist Section |
|---------|-------------------|
| Tag mismatches, orphaned tags, tag case issues | Section 1: Tag Integrity |
| DOCTYPE mismatch, invalid root element, missing attributes | Section 2: DOCTYPE and Topic Structure |
| Nesting/hierarchy errors, crossing tags, invalid element context | Section 3: Nesting and Hierarchy |
| Task elements in wrong topic type | Section 7: Task-Specific Elements |
| List structure errors, empty items, direct text children | Section 6: List Validation |
| Table structure errors, misaligned columns, wrong elements | Section 10: Table Structure |
| Conref/xref path or format issues | Section 12: Cross-References and Links |
| Special character or escaping issues | Section 16: Character Encoding and Special Characters |
